request.spec:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Grace days and auto close are in, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**The setting**
- `grace-days` is a whole number of days, stored on the sheet's row by a new migration, `V36__grace_days.sql`. Blank means off, and it is not dated.
- Saving it writes `SETTING_CHANGED key=grace-days value=<days>` (just `value=` when blank). Anything else is refused with the usual settings error.
- The settings panel has a new field, `setting-grace-days`, and shows the current value in `setting-grace-days-current`. Like the cap, it can be saved blank to turn it off.

**Auto close**
- When the sheet's today is changed, any open period whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, earliest to-date first.
- I moved the close calculation out of `ClosePeriod` into a shared service, `period/PeriodCloser.java`. A close by hand and an auto close now use the same code. An auto close adds ` auto=yes` to the end of its `PERIOD_CLOSED` line.
- The today change (`SaveToday`) runs the auto closes after setting the date and before its rollup lines, so the audit file is in the required order.
- The front end already re-reads the whole sheet after a today change, so newly closed periods show up without any extra code.

**Decision for you:** an auto close skips the role check that a close by hand makes. So if `perm-close` is limited to stewards, a clerk changing today still closes overdue periods. I read "exactly as a close by hand would" as covering the calculation and audit line, not the permission. Viewers can't change today at all, so they can't trigger it. If auto close should respect `perm-close`, it's a one-line check in `PeriodCloser.closeDue`, but it would mean deciding whether a clerk's today change should then be refused or just leave the periods open.
